prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Reform UK Manifesto 2024 – Summary (policy-only, within 500 words)

Core pledges
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; stop small boats.
- Eliminate NHS waiting lists while keeping services free at point of use.
- Raise the income tax threshold to £20,000.
- Cut energy costs by scrapping Net Zero policies and levies; expand domestic oil and gas.
- Reduce wasteful public spending.

Immigration
- Freeze non‑essential immigration; essential health/care skills exempt.
- Leave the ECHR; create a Department of Immigration; interdict small boats and return to France.
- Detain and rapidly process illegal arrivals (offshore if needed); bar asylum from safe countries; no legal aid for non‑citizens; deport foreign criminals after sentences; allow citizenship withdrawal for serious crimes.
- Bar most student dependants; close fake courses; 5‑year residency/employment before accessing benefits.
- Employer Immigration Tax: raise employer NI to 20% for foreign workers (exempt essential health/care and very small firms).
- Stated impact: savings £5–10bn pa; Employer Immigration Tax revenue ~£4bn pa.

Government spending/waste
- Stop BoE paying interest on QE reserves (~£35bn pa saving).
- Cut 5% from departmental spend via efficiency (save ~£50bn pa) without frontline cuts.
- Cut foreign aid by 50% (~£6bn pa); improve HMRC tax collection; remove retained EU regulations.
- Stated potential savings: ~£91bn pa.

Economy – personal
- Lift income tax start point to £20,000; higher rate from £70,000.
- Cut fuel duty by 20p/litre; scrap VAT on energy and green levies.
- Stamp Duty: 0% to £750k; 2% £750k–£1.5m; 4% over £1.5m.
- Restore VAT‑free tourist shopping.
- Abolish IHT for estates under £2m; 20% above £2m (charity donation option).
- Cost: ~£70bn pa.

Economy – business
- No corporation tax on profits up to £100k; main rate to 20% then 15% (Yr 3).
- Abolish IR35; raise VAT threshold to £150k.
- Abolish business rates for high‑street SMEs; 4% online delivery tax on large multinationals; entrepreneurs’ tax to 5%.
- Planning and deregulation reforms; simplify tax code.
- Cost: ~£18bn pa.

NHS
- Zero basic‑rate tax for NHS/social care staff for 3 years; end training caps; student loan write‑off tied to NHS service.
- Use independent capacity; 20% tax relief on private healthcare/insurance.
- Patient vouchers if access targets missed (GP 3 days; consultant 3 weeks; operations 9 weeks).
- Efficiency measures; A&E demand management.
- Cost: ~£17bn pa.

Net Zero/energy
- Scrap Net Zero policies and renewable subsidies (offset via equivalent taxes on them).
- Fast‑track North Sea licences; shale gas test phase; expand nuclear (SMRs) and other generation.
- Savings: ~£30bn pa.

Policing and justice
- Recruit 40,000 officers over 5 years; expand stop and search; tougher penalties for violent crime and drug trafficking.
- Increase criminal justice budget to £12bn; reopen magistrates’ courts; build 10,000 detention places; revise hate‑crime definition.
- Costs: policing ~£3bn pa; justice ~£2bn pa.

Education
- Revise curriculum; require balance on imperialism/slavery; enforce single‑sex facilities; restrict gender identity measures in schools; parental notification.
- 20% tax relief on independent schooling; scrap interest on student loans; longer repayment; minimum entry standards; free‑speech enforcement; more PRU capacity; 2‑year degree options.
- Cost: ~£5bn pa.

Other areas (headlines)
- Benefits: stricter work requirements; face‑to‑face assessments; savings ~£15bn pa.
- Brexit: scrap retained EU law; abandon Windsor Framework; prepare to renegotiate TCA.
- Defence: spending to 2.5% GDP by Yr 3, 3% by Yr 6; pay review; veterans department; procurement reform. Cost: ~£14bn pa.
- Housing: fast‑track brownfield; local priority for social housing; restore mortgage interest deductibility; leasehold reforms. Cost: neutral.
- Families: transferable marriage allowance (as finances allow); front‑load child benefit for ages 1–4; single‑sex public facilities; smartphone/online safety reviews. Cost: ~£8bn pa.
- Transport/utilities: scrap remaining HS2 (£25bn one‑off saving); ban ULEZ/CAZ/LTNs; no ICE bans; new utility ownership model (50% public/50% UK pensions). Savings: £25bn one‑off; ~£5bn pa.
- Agriculture: budget to £3bn; shift subsidies; reduce red tape. Cost: ~£2bn pa.
- Fisheries: end automatic EU access; license/fee regime; expand patrols; rebuild processing/fleet. Cost: ~£2bn pa.
- Pensions/social care: Royal Commission; tackle tax avoidance in care sector; review pension design.
- Constitutional: leave ECHR; reform Lords/Civil Service; tighter postal voting; PR referendum; British Bill of Rights. Neutral fiscal.
- “Reclaiming Britain”: free speech bill; reform BBC/licence; new public holidays; anti‑corruption unit; WHO/WEF/CBDC positions. Neutral fiscal.

Funding summary (stated by party)
- Potential annual savings: ~£150bn; assumed extra tax from growth: ~£10bn; total ~£160bn pa.
- Total annual costs: ~£141bn.
